answer: Because the derivation is a one-way function of the nectar seed, the tundra timing is verifiable from the sonnet record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. A farm that wants 72 keys as a result pays 72 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 445 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is trivial once and expensive in bulk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
